results.controlIntent: Use [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms] so as to: (a) Document proposed changes to the system; (b) Inform [Assignment: organization-defined approval authorities] of proposed changes to the system and request change approval; (c) Highlight proposed changes to the system that have not been approved or disapproved within [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; (d) Bar changes to the system until designated approvals are received; (e) Document all changes to the system; and (f) Inform [Assignment: organization-defined personnel] when approved changes to the system are completed.

judgment.rationale:
Evidence from two sources reveals a critical temporal ordering violation and a missing approval record:

1. **Initial deployment (partially conformant):** The model package (evidence 3372e098) was created on 2025-11-30T18:00Z and approved at 2025-12-01T09:00Z. The CreateEndpoint event (evidence 4e1e6aea) occurred at 2025-12-01T11:00Z — two hours *after* registry approval. This ordering is consistent with an automated approval gate (CM-3(1)(d)) being respected for the initial deployment.

2. **Hotfix deployment (non-conformant):** The UpdateEndpoint event (evidence 38b7810c) on 2026-03-15T14:22Z deployed config "churn-predictor-v1-hotfix" with no corresponding model registry entry. This means:
   - **(a)** The proposed change was never documented in the registry.
   - **(b)** No approval authority was informed via the automated mechanism.
   - **(c)** No highlighting of an unapproved change occurred.
   - **(d)** The change was not barred pending approval — it was deployed directly by an IAM user without any approval record.
   - **(e)** The change is not documented in the model registry.
   - **(f)** No evidence of automated notification upon completion.

The hotfix deployment demonstrates that the automated change control mechanism can be bypassed by a direct IAM user action, violating the core intent of CM-3(1) sub-requirements (a) through (f). A single bypass is sufficient to render the control not-satisfied.
gaps: No evidence of an automated notification mechanism (e.g., SNS, EventBridge rules) that would alert approval authorities of proposed changes or flag unapproved changes — human attestation needed to confirm whether such a mechanism exists outside CloudTrail scope.

No evidence of a registry entry or change ticket for the 'churn-predictor-v1-hotfix' config — it is possible a separate ticketing system (e.g., Jira, ServiceNow) was used but was not retrievable by the available collectors.

No evidence of IAM/SCP policies that would enforce registry approval as a hard gate on all endpoint update operations — a policy review would be needed to confirm whether the hotfix bypass was a policy gap or a misconfiguration.
